title: I made a dice roguelite where every hero is deeply flawed. The barbarian cries after every kill.
author: Quill__581
selftext:
Hi! This is Dice & Bone, a silly dice-placement roguelite inspired by tabletop RPGs.

You roll dice each turn and place them into moves. There are 7 heroes and each one is broken in a different way: a blind archer, an allergic wizard, a skeleton who keeps falling apart, a bard whose exaggerations sometimes work...

60+ stacking relics, so building something completely broken is the whole point. Also there's a three-headed goose boss.

It's free and plays in the browser (works best on mobile):

https://quill-581.itch.io/dice-bone

I'd love feedback, especially on balance. If you find a combo that feels illegal, tell me!

comments.author: StaticAnchor
comments.body:
Thanks for sharing.

Just tried it out, a couple of thoughts.

Any game I play with dice, I want to control the rolling of it. The fact we enter battle with the dice already rolled, you lose that tension of...oh will I roll what I need?

As far as attacks, I only tried the archer, it was a little confusing to understand how the dice worked with the slots. I got it eventually, like dice larger than 5 would work, but having it right next to attack scores felt confusing. Right now it sort of feels..pre determined where certain rolls should go? It could be cool combine the dice to get a large score to go into one slot, or do you want to spread it out across attack/defense/spells etc.

Small thing but going through the tutorial once in combat, it loops again, should get rid of it after the first wave.

Otherwise an interesting concept. I played something similar with dice and there's definitely potential in this space. I'd focus on what makes your dice roguelite different than everything else. What's a purely fun mechanic that keeps you with the game?

Good luck!

replies.author: Quill__581
replies.body:
Thanks a lot for actually playing it and writing all this, really helpful!

Rolling the dice yourself: that's a fair point. Right now the dice are rolled automatically at the start of each turn, but I can see how a "roll" moment would add tension. I'll experiment with that.

Slots: yeah, the requirement (like "5+") sitting right next to the damage number is confusing, I'll make them easier to tell apart.

Combining dice: funny you mention it, the Sensitive Barbarian can actually smash two dice together into one big number! Each hero has its own twist (the bard can "exaggerate" a die, the paladin can run away from fights, etc.), but the archer doesn't show that well. Clearly I need to communicate it better.

The tutorial looping is a bug, thanks for catching it. Fixing it soon.

And good question about what makes it different. For me it's the heroes being flawed in ways that change how you play, plus relics that stack into ridiculous combos. But your comment makes me think I need to show that a lot faster.

Thanks again, and good luck with your own projects!

replies.author: StaticAnchor
replies.body: Oh, maybe on the preview screen for selecting them, you watch them interact with the dice. Like seeing the barbarian smash two dice together and make one and then just wait for you to select with a short description could really help sell it. I would make their effects work almost immediately so you can feel the gameplay different from the very first roll.

replies.author: Quill__581
replies.body: That's a great idea, honestly. Showing it instead of explaining it would sell each hero way better. I'll work on little looping previews on the hero select screen (the barbarian smashing dice, the wizard sneezing mid-spell...). Thanks for coming back with more thoughts!
